summary: This work demonstrates a surface code implementation on a regular 2D hexagonal lattice achieving up to 4.5× the encoding rate of a rotated surface code patch by dense packing of twist defects with optimal 6-layer stabilizer measurement and no distance-reducing hook errors. Applied to chemically accurate ground state energy estimation of utility-scale molecules like the 108-spin-orbital FeMoco nitrogen fixation catalyst, the approach enables solution in under a month using only 89 k noisy qubits at $10^{-3}$ error rate, representing 36× space and 6.6× spacetime improvement over prior Toffoli-minimized designs.
motivation: The surface code's low encoding rate of $2d^2 - 1$ physical qubits per logical qubit becomes a severe bottleneck for utility-scale quantum chemistry problems requiring 100+ spin-orbitals and code distances up to 27, necessitating millions of physical qubits. Twist defects theoretically enable higher rates but have been impractical due to heavy-weight stabilizers, circuit depth, or distance loss.
method: The authors implement surface code twist defects on a degree-3 hex grid using subsystem measurement of lower-weight gauge operators in 6 optimal layers (4 CX + reset + measurement), enabling dense packings: 3-qubit rectangles at 1.5× rate, twist-defect grids at 2× asymptotic rate, and 1D yoked concatenation with $[[n,n-2,2]]$ parity checks at up to 4.5× rate. Extensive circuit-level noise benchmarks in the uniform $10^{-3}$ depolarizing model validate logical error scaling using Stim and sparse-blossom MWPM decoding.
result: Memory error rate for Z-top patches: $p_\mathrm{dynamic}(d) = 10^{-1}(3.5^{-d/10})$; lattice surgery: $10^{-1}(3.5^{-d/30})$ per round. Three-qubit rectangles achieve empirical error matching single-qubit Z-top patches. Dense twist storage with parity check yoking exhibits logical error $\sim (n_\mathrm{row}^2/T_\mathrm{yoke})\,p_\mathrm{dynamic}^2(d)$ yielding effective distance $\sim 2d$ while reducing physical footprint from $3.2\times10^6$ qubits to $8.9\times10^4$ qubits for FeMoco-54 at 1 µs cycle time.
